transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez, Jordan Lee, Maya Chen (Redwood); Mark Rios, Lena Ortiz, Samir Patel, Priya Nair (Emberly).

Summary (auto-generated): Weekend eval run shows 4.3% regressions vs baseline; NER prompt family shows highest FP/precision drop. Action items captured.

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we got about 45 minutes, quick round of intros, Jordan and I are here from Redwood, Maya will hop off after the first 10 to hand off to you for infra details later.
[00:18] Mark: Yep thanks Ava, Mark here, we'll, uh, jump right in — busy week so appreciate the sync.
[00:25] Jordan: Cool, I'll share my screen in a sec — showing the eval dashboard from the weekend run, we pushed the new prompt pruning and the tightened scoring threshold set C.
[00:38] Speaker 1: (background noise)
[00:45] Jordan: alright, so top-line: baseline weekend across your scenario set was 1.2% false positive rate on entity suppression; current run bumped to 5.5% on that family, that's the regression we want to dig into.
[01:05] Lena: That's... larger than we expected. Did you change any guardrail heuristics or was it just the prompt updates?
[01:12] Jordan: Primarily prompt pruning + one small tweak to the safety classifier threshold intended to reduce over-blocking, ironically that opened some edge cases for NER hallucinations.
[01:24] Samir: Can you show an example? Because from our side a lot of the failing cases are proper names that the model is confidently rewriting or annotating incorrectly.
[01:35] Jordan: Yep, pulling sample 14 from the run now — here's the customer note: 'Driver Mauricio Reyes reported delay', model labeled 'Maurice Rios' and redacted differently. You can see token-level probs drop in the span.
[01:49] Ava: Important to note, we did enable KV-cache sharing for this batch which slightly changes sampling dynamics in long-context cases, that might interact with the NER prompt templates.
[02:01] Priya: Wait KV-cache? From a security perspective we need to confirm there is no cross-tenant leakage, did you run it in dedicated mode or hosted?
[02:12] Jordan: This was on the Dedicated test pool you provisioned — isolation is per-tenant, but cache behavior affects token prediction. We'll share the isolation logs, but it should be safe.
[02:24] Priya: Safe, yes, but we still need KMS rotation details and proof of audit logs — our compliance team flagged that as a blocker for production.
[02:34] Ava: Absolutely, that's on the next steps list — we'll send the KMS docs and audit retention timelines.
[02:40] Mark: Back to quality — is it possible the pruning removed crucial prompt context that helped the model disambiguate names?
[02:49] Jordan: Exactly, pruning removed a lightweight disambiguation hint in 18% of the test prompts. Our hypothesis is the hint forced better alignment; removing it reduced precision for span classification.
[03:03] Samir: So two levers: re-introduce the disambiguation hint to the prompt or tighten the guardrail scoring to be more conservative on redaction. Both affect cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:15] Lena: What's the latency delta for reintroducing the hint? If it just adds a couple tokens, maybe ok.
[03:22] Jordan: Token count increases by roughly 12 tokens per request, which for your volume projects to ~6% token cost increase. Latency impact negligible for p95.
[03:33] Mark: Price matter — cost deltas ok if it reduces manual review. But we need to quantify manual review reduction and show ROI.
[03:42] Ava: We'll add a short token-economics doc to the pricing note — quick table mapping token add vs monthly cost vs estimated review cycles avoided.
[03:51] Jordan: Also, regarding the safety classifier tweak — we can restore previous threshold and instead apply per-route exceptions for your NER route so we don't affect other flows.
[04:03] Samir: That sounds good as a canary step.
[04:08] Speaker 1: (brief overlap)
[04:12] Jordan: For the regression hunt we propose a bisection: run A with the hint re-introduced, run B with classifier threshold restored, run C with both, compare. We'll tag the runs and produce a diff heatmap.
[04:25] Samir: I'll prepare the NER prompt family subset and mark golden outputs for 20 examples.
[04:30] Priya: On the compliance ask — can you confirm whether audit logs include per-token traceability? We need to show an event for redaction decisions.
[04:40] Jordan: Current audit logs include request/response metadata, decision flags and model variant, but not raw token stream by default — we can enable a more verbose trace for your pilot under a controlled retention window.
[04:54] Priya: That would help. Also need KMS key rotation frequency and whether HSM-backed keys supported.
[05:02] Ava: We'll include KMS/HSM details in the doc and call out retention windows.
[05:08] Mark: Another thing — we saw a cluster of failures at long-context lengths in the weekend run. Could that be the batching behavior?
[05:18] Jordan: Possibly. We adjusted continuous batching to improve throughput; at long context the batching can increase effective sequence length variance and push kernel selection into a different path, which may yield slightly different output distributions.
[05:32] Lena: So does that mean dedicated vs hosted behaves differently? Because our infra team cares about parity.
[05:40] Jordan: Behavior should be consistent but runtime heuristics differ. We'll produce a parity doc showing kernel/quantization profiles across Dedicated test pool vs Hosted baseline.
[05:52] Samir: Any quick mitigations we can do now? A safe approach might be to pin model variant and disable cache sharing for the NER route while we test.
[06:02] Jordan: Yes that's a low-friction experiment. We can run that overnight and compare.
[06:08] Ava: Ok — let's talk about the rollback drill. If a rollout causes a spike, we want to exercise canary then immediate fallback to previous model variant. We recommend doing a dry-run with traffic split 5/95 then simulate a failure.
[06:22] Mark: We need the playbook in writing — who hits what toggle, how long, and the incident comms.
[06:28] Jordan: We'll provide a step-by-step rollback playbook and a runbook for the SREs.
[06:33] Speaker 1: (auto-label again) / background typing
[06:38] Priya: On security again, can Redwood provide attestation of SOC2 scope and whether logs are forwarded to our SIEM via syslog or cloud provider native connectors?
[06:48] Ava: Yes, we have SOC2 docs and syslog/forwarding options; we'll send the SOC2 cert and the connector matrix.
[06:55] Mark: Great. One more question — any change to latency p95 during the weekend run? We noticed occasional spikes.
[07:03] Jordan: The p95 for NER route increased by 40ms during the batching experiment; baseline was 210ms, now 250ms. For your SLA target of 300ms p95 it's still within range, but noted.
[07:18] Lena: Ok. For our execs, we'll need a short one-pager that summarizes risk, mitigations, and recommended production config.
[07:26] Ava: We'll do a one-pager and include suggested production knobs (pin variant, disable cache, refined prompt) with cost impacts.
[07:33] Samir: One small ask — can Redwood run a quick adversarial pass on the prompt set to surface potential hallucination vectors?
[07:41] Jordan: We can run adversarial augmentation for ~2k synthetic cases overnight, give you the top failure modes. That will help tune guardrails.
[07:50] Mark: Timeline wise — if we get the bisection output and the 20 failing examples by Friday (16th), we can decide whether to proceed with a rollback drill the following week.
[08:01] Ava: That matches our plan. Any blockers?
[08:05] Priya: Only pending the KMS/HSM confirmation and audit log retention commitment.
[08:11] Ava: We'll prioritize those docs.
[08:15] Jordan: Quick note — competitor mention: you asked about Anthropic earlier, our difference there is the runtime optimizations and unified rollback tooling, we can write a short competitive note if helpful.
[08:26] Mark: Yeah send that.
[08:29] Maya Chen: (closing) Thanks everyone — I'll drop the meeting notes into CRM and tag action items.
[08:35] Ava: Thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and the bisection plan.

End of transcript.
